summary.intent: Win the Lio 'Keep the Line Running' hackathon challenge by analyzing Soony's confidential launch data, then building a general recheck-and-act agent product (poller, extraction, recompute, supplier emails with approvals) and preparing demo, pitch and interview material before the Sunday 12:00 hand-in.
summary.outcome: Found that Soony's plan hid real shortfalls (overbooked art books, failed statues, slow Collector's packing), built and deployed the product with sign-off, phone-alert bridge, live and demo instances, README and demo script, and rehearsed all three demo stories. The latest phone-bridge work was being committed and many commits remained unpushed.

repo: Confidential portal data lives in gitignored data/ (raw, drops, notes, img); .env holds SOONY_PORTAL_TOKEN and is gitignored, .env.example is committed.

Portal API has only three endpoints (files list, single file, archive.zip) with no webhooks; changes must be detected by polling and comparing SHA-256, and existing files can be replaced under the same name.
Team workflow files CLAUDE.md and PROGRESS.md exist; work is claimed with a Now line in PROGRESS.md.

Live instance runs on :8000 and demo instance on :8001 via scripts/demo.sh (reset, snapshot, stop; CALLS=twilio switches real calls). Demo uses dry-mail mode so supplier emails are only recorded in data/demo/state/dry_outbox.json.
Live and demo servers share one alert database, so alert-to-case links are stored per state folder.
Web UI polls state every 5 s (POLL_MS=5000) and routines every 15 s; there is no server push.
Phone calls default to ASK_CALL_PROVIDER=dry_run; real Twilio calls cost about $0.38/min; ASK_PUBLIC_URL must be set for keypad/voice webhooks; ASK_CARD_ALERTS=off disables the case-alert bridge.
Entire only writes a checkpoint when repo files change; no-change turns log 'skipping checkpoint', and checkpoints are pushed with git push.
Sign-off flow: one-time /ok/<token> links bypass basic auth (basic_auth.py), approve runs through api.approve with via='signoff'.

code.finding: AlertBook.decide now forwards phone decisions to the linked case via the new card_alerts bridge, applied exactly once.
New bridge raises one alert per red or near-deadline case untouched for 15 min, applies phone decisions to cases, and closes alerts when the case is decided elsewhere.
The background escalation loop runs the card-alert bridge before its usual tick every 30 s.
Implements one-time sign-off links, push/Teams delivery, and simulation fallback via ASK_SIGNOFF_SIMULATE.

workflow: Delegating independent builds and cross-checks (200 order confirmations, 59 scans, sign-off loop, phone bridge) to subagents while writing docs in parallel saved significant time.
Verify UI changes in a real browser on the demo instance (e.g., pressing J ten times and counting highlighted rows) rather than trusting type checks alone.
Ask before spending money (Twilio calls) and before outward-facing actions; keep real supplier emails off the demo instance.
Keep confidential data out of code, docs sent to external services, and the repo; README avoids challenge numbers because the repo goes to the jury.
Check for concurrent edits on shared docs before rewriting sections.

friction: Cloudflare Error 1033 on the demo hostname after the DNS record was first routed to the wrong tunnel; fixed by re-routing.
A race in the shared mailbox sync wrote back a stale action log and lost the 07:58 art-book approval record; fixed with an append-under-lock and restored from the Sent folder.
J/K navigation walked through folded cases individually, so the row highlight vanished and order seemed to jump.
Safari caches favicons stubbornly, so a versioned link was needed.
Rev B case sentence dropped the order number and began with 'usable, but …'.
Servers on :8000 and :8001 needed a restart to pick up new backend code, otherwise the done screen was stale.
Push notifications go to every subscribed phone, with no per-person targeting.
The assistant's earlier note that the Entire SessionStart was logged under a different session ID was a minor oddity; Codex hooks still need approval in /hooks.
open_items: Several commits unpushed, including the phone bridge, the demo script and the ⌘↵ shortcut work; the phone-bridge commit was still in progress.
Restart live and demo servers to load the phone bridge; consider ASK_CARD_ALERTS=off on live to avoid dry-run alerts in the shared DB.
Register sender email addresses in the portal Settings and decide on a team inbox so supplier mail can really be sent and replied to.
Optional: 'What still saves it' section on Launch, replaying supplier replies on the demo, folding the count questions, and Maren's top bar saying 'nothing needs you'.
Delete the duplicate routine (awaiting user decision) and decide whether to delete the earlier Claude doc.
Hand-in tasks before 12:00: video, pitch deck, final demo rehearsal; run scripts/demo.sh reset before each rehearsal and the pitch.
Question for Felix at the 09:00 office hours about who gets the container to the DC; write down a quote for the 'Felix told us…' moment.
Rotate the portal login that was pasted into Discord after the hack.
Phone alerts for already-overdue red cases could cost money with real calls; tune ASK_CALL_AFTER_MIN and ASK_CALL_MAX_OPEN.
